terms.meaning: an Excel file containing one or more sheets
one tab of data inside a workbook
a Python library for working with tables
the library pandas uses to write .xlsx files

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and logger setup
sections.what: Loads pandas for tables, typing and path and date helpers, and the logger.

sections.name: ExcelExporter (part 1)
sections.title: Creating the workbook and summary sheet
sections.what: Creates the output folder if it is missing, opens an Excel file, and writes a Summary sheet with the question, answer, timestamp and counts of sources and evidence, then sets column widths.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a one-glance record of each answer.
sections.watch_out: Column widths are set by turning column numbers into letters with a simple formula that only works up to 26 columns.

sections.name: ExcelExporter (part 2)
sections.title: Writing the sources and evidence sheets
sections.what: Adds a Sources sheet with rank, file, location, link, path and relevance, and an Evidence sheet with the text of each piece, its score and modified date. Each sheet is added only when there is data.
sections.why: Gives full evidence to check the answer against.
sections.watch_out: Evidence text is cut to 500 characters, so the full passage is not in the spreadsheet.

sections.name: ExcelExporter (part 3)
sections.title: Finishing evidence layout and starting multi-query export
sections.what: Makes the content column on the Evidence sheet wide and ends the single-result export. Then it starts the multi-query export by building one row per query: number, question, shortened answer, confidence, and counts of sources and evidence.
sections.why: Lets several results be compared in one file.
sections.watch_out: The answer is cut to 200 characters on the All Queries sheet, so long answers are truncated there.

sections.name: ExcelExporter (part 4)
sections.title: Final sizing and saving the multi-query sheet
sections.what: Sets column widths for the All Queries sheet, capped at 60, saves the file and returns its path. Any error is logged and raised again.
sections.why: Same column tidy-up as the other sheets.
sections.watch_out: Errors are raised again, so the caller must handle them or the request will fail.

summary: Writes query answers, sources and evidence into Excel workbooks, either one query per file or many queries in one file.
purpose: Gives users a spreadsheet record of answers they can filter, sort and share.
why: Likely reason: spreadsheets are familiar to most business users for reviewing results.
how: export_query_result creates a workbook with Summary, Sources and Evidence sheets, sets column widths, and saves it. export_multiple_queries builds an All Queries sheet with one row per query and saves it.
inputs: The query text, answer, source records, evidence records, confidence values, and an output file path.
outputs: An Excel file at the output path, and that path returned.
risks: Column widths use a simple letter formula that only works for the first 26 columns. Evidence is cut to 500 characters and answers to 200 in the summary sheet. Errors are logged and raised again, so the caller must handle them.
debug: If a file is not created, check the output path and whether the folder can be written. If columns look wrong, count the columns on the sheet. If evidence text is short, that is the 500 character cut.
